tier_reason: First-party Microsoft README table (onnxruntime/python/tools/transformers/README.md) with public driver scripts (run_benchmark.sh, benchmark.py, models/gpt2/benchmark_gpt2.py) and stated GPU/CPU (Tesla V100-PCIE-16GB, Xeon E5-2690 v4), but both engines are prebuilt packages (onnxruntime-gpu 1.4.0, PyTorch 1.5.1) with no CUDA, cuDNN or driver version and no pinned script commit, so it is not A; same treatment as CTranslate2 and other prebuilt-wheel entries (C).

corrections.compiler_and_flags: Not built from source: prebuilt onnxruntime-gpu 1.4.0 against PyTorch 1.5.1 TorchScript, so no compiler or flags; CUDA, cuDNN and driver versions are not stated. Stated settings: IO binding enabled, ORT transformer optimizer script (graph fusion), fp32 and fp16 ORT rows, run through run_benchmark.sh (benchmark.py) and the benchmark_gpt2.py commands printed in the README; the script commit behind the 2020 table is not pinned.
corrections.caveats: Numbers are from ORT 1.4.0 and PyTorch 1.5.1 (2020 era); newer PyTorch (torch.compile, SDPA kernels) and newer ORT are not in the table, so the gap today is unknown. The baseline is TorchScript only (no TensorRT, no PyTorch eager row), and TorchScript appears only at batch 1; the batch 4 (BERT) and batch 8-128 (GPT-2) rows are ORT-only. The advantage shrinks to 1.2x at s=512 batch 1. The fp16 rows are ORT fp16 against the TorchScript fp32 row; the current benchmark.py can run TorchScript in fp16 (model.half(), '-e torchscript -g -p fp16') but the table shows no such row, so the 6.6x fp16 figure compares unequal precisions. The README table is for bert-base-uncased while the current run_benchmark.sh default model list is bert-base-cased, roberta-base and distilbert-base-uncased with sequence lengths up to 1024, so the exact script version behind the table is not pinned. First-party (Microsoft) measurement on prebuilt packages with no CUDA/cuDNN/driver versions. The README states the results were obtained with the optimizer and IO binding enabled. Weak independent corroboration (not used for the tier): ELS-RD/transformer-deploy (Apache-2.0, 1.7k stars) README reports ONNX Runtime FP32 below PyTorch FP32 latency on an RTX 3090 (MiniLM-L6 classification 1.57 vs 5.43 ms; gpt2 4.99 vs 9.43 ms) with no batch size or versions, and its question-answering block duplicates the token-classification numbers exactly.

notes: All quoted numbers and derived ratios match the README tables (5.7x, 3.1x, 1.2x, 6.6x fp16-vs-fp32, GPT-2 4.1x). Downgraded A to C: first-party run on prebuilt wheels without CUDA/cuDNN versions or a pinned script commit; shortcomings to record are the 2020-era versions, TorchScript-only batch-1 baseline, fp16 ORT compared against fp32 TorchScript, and the unpinned script version. Metadata (MIT, 22.0k stars, last commit 2026-10-10, active) checked and correct.

tier_reason: The claim (BAM read-write loop 5x faster, BAM to SAM 13x faster, both at 16 threads vs Samtools 0.1.19) is the abstract of the peer-reviewed GigaScience 2021 paper (giab007), reproduced verbatim in the repo README's BibTeX entry; the paper is first-party but peer-reviewed, so B. Full text, hardware, compiler and tables were unreachable, so it cannot be A.
notes: Abstract numbers verified in the README; the paper full text (doi.org, OUP, PMC, bioRxiv, eprints.gla.ac.uk) was unreachable from this environment (ENOTFOUND/blocked), so per-tool comparisons against HTSJDK, Sambamba and Scramble mentioned in the record could not be checked. Shortcomings: baseline is HTSlib's own predecessor (Samtools 0.1.19), not an independent competitor; the 16-thread setting means much of the gain is threading; no hardware or compiler visible. Category 'genomics-file-formats' is not one of wave 8's seven categories (nearest existing ones: wave 11 filesystems-and-io or wave 4 binary-schemas); the orchestrator should re-file it with a category override. Metadata checked: MIT/Expat outside cram/ and Modified 3-Clause BSD inside cram/ (LICENSE), 953 stars, default branch develop, last commit 2026-10-08, active.

tier_reason: benchmark/performance_v320.md gives compiler (MSVC 19.51, Release, default CMake options), CPU (Ryzen 9 9950X3D) and method, and the v3.2 side runs public code (benchmark/main.c, shared/benchmarks.c), but the v3.1.1 baseline column ran an unpublished port of the v3.2 scenes: v3.1.1's own shared/benchmarks.c and benchmark/main.c contain only 7 of the 14 scenes (no compounds, junkyard, washer, queries, tree_cast, tile_world or sleep) and run spinner for 1400 steps instead of 500, so the baseline cannot be reproduced from public code; first-party partial methodology is C.

corrections.caveats: SELF-COMPARISON: the baseline is the project's own previous release (v3.1.1), not another engine; Box2D is 2D only, so ODE and Bullet (3D) are not comparable and the repo contains no comparison against any other engine. v3.2 is unreleased (latest tag v3.1.1, 2025-06-04); the numbers come from the main branch, and performance_v320.md was added in commit ac7c751 on 2026-10-04. The baseline column is not reproducible from public code: the page says v3.1.1 ran the v3.2 scenes 'ported to the v3.1.1 API without changing them', but that port is not published, and the v3.1.1 tag's own benchmark app has only 7 of the 14 scenes (joint_grid, large_pyramid, many_pyramids, rain, smash, spinner, tumbler) with spinner at 1400 steps versus 500 on main. The page says 'These are relative numbers from one machine. Read the ratios, not the milliseconds.' v3.1.1 used enkiTS for threading while v3.2 uses its built-in scheduler, and v3.2 creates fewer contacts because of a tighter broad-phase AABB margin (washer 29k vs 42k contacts, tumbler 8.6k vs 11k), so the work per step is not identical (the page counts that as an engine improvement). Single machine (Windows 11, MSVC); the per-machine CSV folders (amd7950x_avx2, amd7950x_sse2, amd7950x_float, m2air_float, m2air_neon, n100_sse2) were not opened. Independent but weak extra evidence (not used for the tier): Ughuuu/benchmarks-repo docs/REPORT-2D.md (Godot 4.7-stable, 300 timed steps, 60 Hz, single run, step p50, no CPU model stated) measures Box2D through a Godot addon against GodotPhysics2D and Rapier2D: pyramid 24.06 ms vs 151.83 ms (GodotPhysics2D) and 19.47 ms (Rapier2D wins); mixed_pile 5.91 vs 64.78 and 8.77 ms; joint_grid 3.83 ms vs 7.99 ms (Rapier2D; GodotPhysics2D failed) but Box2D's displacement_max is inf; smash 11.52 vs 12.42 (Rapier2D) and 50.63 ms; query_storm 4.28 vs 7.11 and 63.39 ms; drop 21.10 vs 17.81 ms (Rapier2D wins) and 117.37 ms. That run includes Godot addon overhead and is not a clean engine comparison.

notes: Every quoted number (14-scene table, 2.04x/2.19x geometric means, SSE2-forced 1.83x/2.03x, AVX2 about 10%) matches performance_v320.md, and the third-party Godot numbers in caveats match REPORT-2D.md. Downgraded A to C because half the scenes in the v3.1.1 baseline column come from an unpublished port; the main shortcoming to record is the self-comparison against the project's own previous release (off-baseline, no other engine). Metadata checked: MIT, 10.4k stars, last commit 2026-10-04, active, not a fork.
